brief.headline: Healthcare leads risk-on tape while Nvidia CEO turmoil rattles tech sector
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits 0.6% below its 50DMA and 4.3% above the 200DMA after a 0.9% weekly loss and 2.3% monthly decline. The regime is still labeled risk-on, but that label is under pressure: XLK is the worst sector on 20-day momentum (-8.4%) while VIX at 19.0 is fractionally below its 20DMA of 19.4, signalling contained but rising anxiety. Breadth is reasonably healthy with 73% of sectors above their 50DMAs, led by Healthcare, Consumer Discretionary and Financials. The Nvidia CEO story breaking today adds an idiosyncratic shock to an already soft tech tape; a breakout in a risk-on market carries more weight in Healthcare right now than in semiconductors.

portfolio.note: Price at $521.13 is 1.8% below the 20DMA and 6.8% off the 20-day high; RSI at 47.7 and 20-day momentum at -2.4% confirm drift. The Nvidia CEO contagion is weighing on the broader XLK sector today, so the 20DMA near $530 is the level to watch for a reclaim.

ASML is in a full bearish MA stack, 10.3% below the 100DMA and 9.2% below its 20-day high. All 19 EPS estimate revisions in the past 30 days went up (zero down), which preserves fundamental support, but Nvidia CEO turmoil is hitting European semis today and the technical picture has deteriorated materially since entry at $820.

XLE at $63.37 is 28% below cost basis and sitting 4.6% under its 20DMA with 20-day momentum of -6.3%. WTI dropped 4% this week and is 9.8% below its 20DMA; a stabilisation in crude above the $84–86 range is needed before the thesis can recover.

GLD at $365.17 is in a bearish MA stack and 5.1% below the 100DMA; gold spot (GC=F) is off 4.9% this week with RSI at 37.2. Despite the drawdown, the position is still up 59% from cost of $230, so this is a sizing and stop question rather than a thesis break.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly and Company
watchlist.thesis: LLY is 7.4% above its 20DMA at $1,437, RSI 70.3, only 1.1% below its 20-day high of $1,453. Revenue estimates have been revised up 3.4% and EPS up 2.3% over the past 30 days. A China regulatory approval for one of its GLP-1 drugs hit wires this morning, adding a catalyst. Healthcare (XLV) is the top sector on 20-day momentum at +8.6%, giving this setup meaningful regime support.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: $1,338. 20-day high: $1,453. ATR-based stop distance: ~$46 (3.2% of price).
watchlist.risk: RSI is overbought at 70.3 and trailing P/E of 46.7x is elevated, so any macro risk-off move or GLP-1 reimbursement headline could snap back sharply.

watchlist.name: Accenture plc
watchlist.thesis: ACN is up 18% over 20 days and 34.8% over 40 days, sitting 1.8% above its 20DMA at $253.66 with RSI 59.6. It leads both the market and its sector on 20-day RS (+19.3% vs market, +26.4% vs sector). Earnings on 17 December are a near-term catalyst; 15 of 23 estimate revisions in 30 days went up. Forward P/E is 15.9x, modest relative to the momentum.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: $249.11. 20-day high: $271.76. ATR-based stop distance: ~$10.20 (4.0% of price).
watchlist.risk: The stock dropped 4% this week despite the strong trend; a close back below the 20DMA at $249 would question momentum sustainability ahead of earnings.

watchlist.name: Texas Instruments Incorporated
watchlist.thesis: TXN is 5.7% above its 20DMA at $309.81, all 23 EPS estimate revisions in the past 30 days were upward with EPS revised +6.2% and revenue +1.9%. Quarterly earnings growth was 106%, and the stock is outperforming the sector by 19.4% over 20 days. A less AI-centric semiconductor name, so less exposure to the Nvidia CEO contagion today.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: $293.05. 20-day high: $317.20. ATR-based stop distance: ~$12.98 (4.2% of price).
watchlist.risk: Trailing P/E of 40.2x is 23% above its historical median; a broader tech sector unwind triggered by the Nvidia story could pull TXN down even if fundamentals are sound.

watchlist.name: ServiceNow, Inc.
watchlist.thesis: NOW has collapsed 26.6% over 20 days and sits 20% below its 20DMA and 35.6% below its 20-day high of $159.50. EPS estimates were cut by 2.8% (34 of 38 revisions were negative). The Anthropic IPO is raising questions about whether independent AI-workflow spending compresses enterprise software multiples. At RSI 31, technically oversold, but the downtrend has no apparent floor yet.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: $128.29. 20-day high: $159.50. ATR-based stop distance: ~$6.72 (6.5% of price).
watchlist.risk: P/E is 40% below historical median at 73.9x trailing, which could attract value buyers and trigger a sharp short-covering bounce that disrupts a bearish position.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: INTC is in a full bearish MA stack, 37.2% below its 100DMA, with 20-day momentum of -36.3%. EPS and revenue estimates were both cut this week (25 of 32 revisions negative), and the stock is dragged further by the Nvidia CEO scandal today. A 7.3% bounce this week is likely a dead-cat move given ATR of $6.02 (9.6% daily range) and no structural improvement.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: $76.96. 20-day high: $96.87. ATR-based stop distance: ~$6.02 (9.6% of price).
watchlist.risk: Any rumour of a strategic deal or asset sale could produce a violent squeeze given the high implied volatility (20-day realised vol 144%); position sizing must reflect the ATR.

watchlist.name: Gilead Sciences, Inc.
watchlist.thesis: GILD sits 4.1% above its 20DMA at $169.73, RSI 62.2, with 20-day momentum of +10.5%. EPS estimates were revised up by an enormous 146% over 30 days, likely reflecting a one-time item, but revenue estimates rose 1.9% as well. Healthcare sector momentum is the strongest in the market right now, and GILD benefits from that tailwind.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: ~$163.10 (implied from +4.1%). 20-day high implied ~$176.6. ATR-based stop distance: ~$4.80 (2.8% of price).
watchlist.risk: The 146% EPS revision is likely a normalisation distortion; if it unwinds, the fundamental case looks far weaker and the stock could reprice quickly.

commodities.name: Natural gas
commodities.note: The standout commodity this week: up 11.9% and 11.8% above its 20DMA with RSI at 63.3. Watch $3.30 as near-term resistance; any seasonal demand pull could extend the move but thin liquidity amplifies vol.

commodities.name: WTI crude
commodities.note: Down 4.0% this week, 9.8% below its 20DMA and 21.4% below the 20-day high with RSI at 38.5; the bearish momentum (-11.3% over 20 days) is weighing on XLE and energy equities broadly. A close back above $90 would be needed to shift the trend.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Gold fell 4.9% this week and sits in a bearish MA stack, 7.3% from its 20-day high with RSI at 37.2. The 20-day momentum of -6.2% and 40-day of -11.1% suggest the correction has further room; watch whether $3,800 provides support.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Copper is flat on the week at $6.20 but down 4.8% over 20 days and 3.6% below its 20DMA; RSI at 38.5 and mixed MA stack signal indecision. As a growth proxy, copper's soft tone aligns with the broader tech and energy weakness.

commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.note: Wheat at $596.75 is in a bearish MA stack with RSI at 31.4 and 20-day momentum of -10.9%; it is 11% below its 20-day high with thin liquidity flagged. No near-term catalyst visible.

risks: Nvidia CEO crisis: board reportedly weighing ousting Jensen Huang; a confirmed leadership change would likely extend the AI-chip selloff and pressure ASML, MSFT and other indirect beneficiaries further.
XLK is the worst sector on 20-day momentum at -8.4%; a continued tech unwind in a nominally risk-on tape creates mixed signals and could drag SPY below the 50DMA decisively.
SPY is only 0.6% below its 50DMA; a weekly close below that level would shift the regime label and invalidate bullish setups in Healthcare and Financials.

Crude oil's 4% weekly drop and 11.3% 20-day momentum decline are compressing energy earnings estimates; XLE is already 28% below portfolio cost basis and further downside is possible if demand signals weaken.
